# Invoice import for a small accounting firm

A three-person accounting firm in Brno handled about 900 supplier invoices a month for 140 clients. Each invoice was retyped from a PDF into the accounting system, which took roughly two minutes, so the team spent close to thirty hours a month on data entry. Most errors came from foreign suppliers, where the due date and the issue date were easy to mix up.

In October we connected the accounting system's invoice reader. It pulls the supplier, the amount, VAT and the due date, and the accountant only confirms that the fields are right. Regular suppliers go through quickly; the first invoice from a new supplier still needs a full check.

After four weeks an invoice takes about twenty seconds. We kept a manual review for documents above 50,000 CZK because a mistake there costs real money. Two clients send photos taken on a phone, and those are still read badly, so we enter them the old way for now.

Next time we would ask suppliers earlier to send invoices in the ISDOC format. The system reads it without errors and the due date check disappears. About a third of suppliers do this today.

The extension costs 4,000 CZK a month plus one day of setup. It saves about twenty-five hours a month, which the accountants now spend on calls with clients. The bigger gain is timing: invoices reach the system the next day, so clients see their cash flow sooner than before.

If you are considering the same step, start with the suppliers who send the most invoices. For us that was five companies, together almost half of all documents.
